title: refactor(driver-sql): move applyDriftOpInPlace's and rebuildSqliteTablePatched's bodies out of sql-driver.ts into sql-driver-schema-sync.ts (#25521 cut 6)
body:

_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X6RcybLaAtijgtf3Zm7ot2z)_

Part of #25521
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Ruling-ref: 6270097840
Ruling-ref: 6348891160

Cut 6 of the `sql-driver.ts` split (#24586 ruling A, recorded in `6270097840`). The claim is `6411690694`. The bodies of the two in-place drift reconcilers of schema sync, the protected `SqlDriver#applyDriftOpInPlace` and `SqlDriver#rebuildSqliteTablePatched`, move unedited into a new seam module, `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-schema-sync.ts`, and reach the class through one named host, `SchemaSyncHost`. Both methods keep their names, docblocks, signatures (less `async`) and positions.

It is move-only, and the card stays open for the later cuts. Branch `claude/project-thread-hq3kec` (platform-assigned to this card thread, as the claim records). The cut commit `381a4bb77d` sits on `origin/main` `05f7758f05`; `origin/main` was then merged in (`ebb210bf1b`, merge base `c16c00f930`). The 17 commits it brought touch no driver package.

**Net line count (the seat's rule from ACCEPT `6385306916`).** `sql-driver.ts` goes from 21,512 lines to 21,398: **-114**. The two bodies are 152 lines; the two stubs are 33 body lines, and the new import with its comment is 5. The new module is 227 lines.

**Serial with the file's in-flight PRs.** Re-measured at my start: 20 open PRs, each file list read in full. None touches `packages/drivers/driver-sql/**`, `driver-turso/**` or `driver-sqlite-wasm/**`, except the Version Packages PR #25640, which touches only those packages' `CHANGELOG.md` and `package.json`. Seat 1's #8740 (`SqlDriver.upsert`) has no open PR yet, and it is a different region; `insertOnlyUpsertColumns` is not touched.

## The area, measured on `05f7758f05`

- `applyDriftOpInPlace` is lines 14859-14919 of `sql-driver.ts` (one-line docblock, 58 body lines). `rebuildSqliteTablePatched` is 14921-15049 (32-line docblock, 94 body lines). Both sit in the Schema sync section of cut 1's seam table, beside the `applyMigrationEntries` that calls them (it stays).
- Both are protected with annotated return types (a promise of a boolean, and a promise of the honoured `ManagedDriftEntry` list), so the inferred-return limit does not bite.
- Neither builds through `getBuilder`, so `check:tenant-chokepoint` rule 1 is untouched (24 bindings across 3 files at both ends).
- Neither reads a static: an AST screen of the two bodies finds no `SqlDriver.` read and no cast-wrapped `this` read. The members they read are exactly `knex`, `logger`, `dialectName`, `isMysql`, `isPostgres`, `managedObjectFields`, `managedObjectIndexes`, and the methods `applyIndexDriftOp`, `introspectColumns`, `buildRebuiltColumn`, `nowColumnDefault`, `applyDeclaredColumnDefault`, `syncTableIndexes` and `resolveTenantField`.
- Neither has a `this.FIELD.delete/insert/update(` site: the one map read is `this.managedObjectFields.get(table)`. `driver-sql` is outside the tenant-audit census corpus anyway (cut 1's reading).
- `TursoDriver` and `SqliteWasmDriver` override none of the two methods or the members they call (`git grep` over both packages' `src`, tests excluded: 0 overrides).

## The shape (#23050 shape B, as cuts 1-5 apply it)

- The class keeps both methods, docblock included, byte-identical except that `async` is dropped. Each body is now one host literal plus a `.call(host, ...)` of the moved function, marked `[#25521 cut 6]`. It returns the moved function's own promise, so a caller awaits the same settlement.
- `SchemaSyncHost` lists the 14 members above, each typed as the class member (an indexed access on `SqlDriver`). Each moved function types its `this` as the Pick of the host over exactly the members its body reads (6 and 10), and each stub annotates its literal as the `ThisParameterType` of the moved function. There is no cast, and no member becomes public.
- The fields `knex`, `logger`, `managedObjectFields` and `managedObjectIndexes`, the getter `dialectName` and the two dialect getters go as GETTERS that read the driver at call time. The methods go as late-bound closures that call them on the driver, so a subclass override or an instance spy is still the one the body reaches.
- `this.logger.warn(...)` keeps its receiver: the getter hands back the driver's logger object and `warn` is called on it (the cut 2 shape, `rawStatementFault`).
- **Module-level declarations.** The bodies read `isIndexDriftOp` and the types `DriftOp` and `ManagedDriftEntry`. All three live in `schema-drift.ts`, which exports them, so the module imports them from there (not a copy). `sql-driver.ts` still reads all three, so its import list does not change. No declaration gains an `export`; `index.ts` re-exports nothing from the new module. The module imports only the type `SqlDriver` from `sql-driver.ts`, so there is no value cycle.
- The move was produced by a script from the source text, not retyped: each body line re-indented two columns. Neither body holds a multi-line template literal, so no line keeps its base indentation.

### Why `resolveHashShadowKeys` stays (the open call this cut was handed)

Measured: its body is 25 lines and reads only `knex` (plus `isHashShadowCarrier` and `parseHashShadowKeyParts` from `schema-drift.ts`; no static), so a stub of about 6 lines would pay about -19. It stays in the class, for two reasons:

- **The claim's file surface names one new or existing seam module.** Its only caller is cut 5's `introspectIndexes` body, so its home is `sql-driver-introspection.ts`; moving it there would edit a second seam module in this PR, and moving it into the new module would put a catalog-read enrichment into the drift-apply module.
- **It shares nothing with this pair** but `knex`, so carrying it would not shrink this cut's host; it is its own slice, priced on its own.

It is proposed below as a small follow-up slice into `sql-driver-introspection.ts`.

### Overrides and spies, measured

- `sql-driver-schema-drift.test.ts` calls `applyDriftOpInPlace` on the driver after replacing `knex` and `logger` on the instance; the getters read the replacements. `sql-driver-unique-tenancy.test.ts` calls `rebuildSqliteTablePatched` on the driver.
- A scratch probe against the built `dist` (not committed) gave 25 readings, **identical at base and at head** (diff empty). It covered: the honoured entries of a SQLite rebuild (relax and drop honoured, widen ignored, the same entry objects); an instance spy on `introspectColumns` (reached once); a subclass overriding `buildRebuiltColumn`, `syncTableIndexes`, `nowColumnDefault` and `resolveTenantField` (each reached, the same calls); columns and rows after the rebuild; a `managedObjectFields` map replaced on the instance after construction (its default re-materialized); an index op routed to a subclass `applyIndexDriftOp`; the SQLite unsupported-op warning through a logger replaced after construction, with `this` bound to the logger; the Postgres arm through a subclass `isPostgres` getter (six op types, the five statements and the `false`); the MySQL arm through a subclass `isMysql` getter (the restated `varchar(40)` and the missing-column `false`); a `knex.raw` that throws synchronously (still a rejected promise at both ends); and a failing `syncTableIndexes` after a rebuild (the same `warn` line).

## The published `.d.ts` does not change

Under the series bar (ruling `6348891160`, letter A), measured on base `05f7758f05` and head `381a4bb77d`, each built with `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql build` against the same dependency tree (the base leg restores the base `sql-driver.ts` and removes the module in this worktree after the cut commit, under an EXIT/INT/TERM trap that restores HEAD; restore proved by blob hash and an empty `git diff HEAD`). Re-read at the merged head `ebb210bf1b`: the same.

- This package emits `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.d.mts` (no `.d.cts`); the two are identical at every end.
- Raw sha256 of both files at base, head and merged head: `93da45168e82136b7613944525e47402d5dc6f9f8daa9efa4bdceeaa11b52a89` (cuts 1-5's hash, unchanged). `cmp` base vs head: identical, so the proof rests on raw identity and no normaliser is relied on.
- Positive control on a copy of the head `dist/index.d.ts`: line 5604, `protected applyDriftOpInPlace(op: DriftOp)`, with `protected` removed, gives `464af7349dba2db4f27756062df5297f44af8deeef3604276d10eee4e6059d9c` and a 4-line diff.
- Export tables: the ESM and CJS bundles each export the same 56 names at base, head and merged head (sorted lists `diff`-identical).
- The head build carries the move: `.call(host` sites in `dist/index.mjs` and `dist/index.js` go 16 to 18.

No changeset: `skip-changeset`, per ruling `6348891160` item 4 (move-only, no product behaviour change).

## Proof of move-only

- **Body, by AST token** (recursive `getChildren` leaves, string and template pieces as their exact source text; comments compared line by line less leading whitespace). For each moved function, the parameters (less the added `this`), return type and body have the same token sequence as the base method, and `async` matches. `applyDriftOpInPlace`: 409 body tokens, 0 differ, 7 comments identical. `rebuildSqliteTablePatched`: 592 body tokens, 0 differ, 33 comments identical.
- **Lines**: 156 lines of the two bodies compared (closing braces included); every one is the base line with two leading spaces removed.
- **Negative control**: in a copy of the module, `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` becomes `PRAGMA foreign_keys = 0FF`. The check then reports 1 token and 1 line different and exits `PROOF FAILED`, exit 1.
- **Class side**: 347 members at base and head, in the same order. The 345 that did not move are byte-identical to base, leading trivia included. Each stub's leading trivia and signature equal the base's, less `async`.
- **Top level of `sql-driver.ts`**: 202 non-class statements at base, 203 at head; all 202 base statements byte-identical at head. The one new statement is the `./sql-driver-schema-sync.js` import with its four-line comment.
- **Size**: +267 / -154 over 2 files, far under the 3,000-line manual-merge line.

## Readers of `sql-driver.ts` by path, checked against the moved text

None needed an edit:

- **ADR anchors.** `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__drivers__driver-sql__src__sql-driver.ts.json` carries ADR-0053 (`formatOutput`, `presentReadValue`) and ADR-0120 D4 (the `recreate_index` ceremony, which lives in `applyIndexDriftOp` and stays). Neither paragraph describes a moved body, so per card ask 3 no entry is owed. The moved bodies cite no ADR. `check:adr-anchors`: 87 anchored files at both ends; decision-letter citations on the anchored surface **1,864 at base (`c16c00f930`, clean detached worktree) and 1,864 at head (`ebb210bf1b`)**.
- **Symbol anchors.** No ADR, checklist or doc anchors `sql-driver.ts#applyDriftOpInPlace` or `#rebuildSqliteTablePatched` (`git grep` over `docs/`, `content/`, `scripts/`, `.github/`: 0 hits). `check:adr-symbol-anchors`: 2,658 anchors resolve at both ends.
- **`check:tenant-chokepoint`.** Rule 1 verdict and population unchanged (above). Rule 2 visits raw-family calls in `SCAN_FILES`; the moved bodies' 13 raw calls (the Postgres and MySQL `ALTER TABLE` statements, the two `PRAGMA foreign_keys` toggles and the rebuild's `INSERT ... SELECT`) are DDL and a copy; none says `IS NULL` against a tenant column. Verdict unchanged; `.raw(` call sites in `sql-driver.ts` go 70 to 57 (see the acceptance notes).
- **Logger receivers.** `check:logger-receiver-detach`: 0 detaches at both ends (3,717 files walked at base, 3,719 at head: the new module and the gitignored generated `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts`, which the unbuilt base worktree lacks). `logger-receiver-detach.test.ts` ③ scans `sql-driver.ts` only; the two moved `this.logger.warn(` calls are direct calls, and the repo-wide gate covers the new module (cut 2's reading).
- **Test comments** that name the two methods (`sql-driver-11321-sqlite-audit-default-canonical.test.ts`, `sql-driver-11722-sqlite-rebuild-applied-honesty.test.ts`, `schema-drift.ts`) and the `{@link rebuildSqliteTablePatched}` references in the class still point at the methods, which are still there. No test reads either body as source text.
- `check:driver-conformance` at base and head: **55 covered, 0 in the DEBT ledger, 0 exempt, both times.**

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` (driver-sql) exit 0. `eslint --no-inline-config` over `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src`: 266 files (the new module included), 0 errors, 0 warnings, exit 0.
- Each suite ran under its own `os-verify-lock` call, exit 0 at every end. Compared per test name and status from vitest's JSON reporter, base `05f7758f05` vs head `381a4bb77d`, and again vs the merged head `ebb210bf1b`:
  - `packages/drivers/driver-sql`: 3,999 tests (3,787 passed, 0 failed, 212 skipped; 247 files) at every end; 0 lost, 0 changed, 0 added.
  - `packages/drivers/driver-turso`, against that end's built driver-sql `dist`: 2,526 tests (2,492 passed, 0 failed, 34 skipped; 95 files); 0 / 0 / 0 (2,513 distinct names).
  - `packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm`: 704 tests (704 passed; 39 files); 0 / 0 / 0.
- `dispatch-gates --commands` on this diff at the merged head `ebb210bf1b` (merge base `c16c00f930`, no STALE TREE): 55 derived commands, each run with its exit code captured before any pipe. `--ran` reconciles 55 derived, 54 run, 1 NOT MEASURED, 0 unrun. The NOT MEASURED one is `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET: it needs every package's `dist`), which CI runs. `check:lean-entry-closure` first exited 3 (no `objectql` dist) and exits 0 after `turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/objectql`.
- Also run, outside the derivation: `check:adr-anchors`, `check:adr-symbol-anchors`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:filter-alias-parity` (rosters under `packages/`), `check:commit-card-trailers` and its `--range origin/main..HEAD` (2 commits, clean): all exit 0.
- No reverse verification or ablation: the diff changes no tested behaviour.

## Acceptance notes

- **`check:tenant-chokepoint` rule 2 reads 13 fewer raw call sites in `sql-driver.ts`.** `SCAN_FILES` names `sql-driver.ts` and not the seam modules, so rule 2 no longer visits the moved DDL calls; the new module holds 13 `.raw(` sites. None is an arm on a tenant column today, but a future edit that added one in the module would not be caught by rule 2. Widening `SCAN_FILES` is a gate edit and the open precondition the series carries for the `getBuilder` areas; it is not made here.
- **Proposed next slices.** (a) `resolveHashShadowKeys` into `sql-driver-introspection.ts` beside its only caller (about -19; `IntrospectionHost` already lists it and `knex`). (b) The rest of the drift-apply family next to this pair, `applyIndexDriftOp` (~14719) and `restoreBareIndexAfterFailedTighten` (~14836), into this cut's module: neither builds through `getBuilder`; both should be screened for statics and priced against the net-line rule at dispatch, and `applyIndexDriftOp` carries the ADR-0120 D4 ceremony, so its anchor entry paragraph would follow it into a new entry for the module.
- The class methods now return the moved functions' promises instead of being `async` methods. A caller awaits the same settlement, and a synchronous throw inside a body still arrives as a rejection (probe reading above).
